transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Iranian forces say they launched a retaliatory attack on a U.S. radar system on an airbase
in Bahrain overnight.
It's the second such attack since Friday.
NPR's Ayah Batrawi has more from Dubai.
Iran's state media reported the sound of explosions in Iranian territory near the street
of Hormuz after midnight Sunday without elaborating further.
Soon after, Iran's Revolutionary Guard issued a statement saying it had delivered a "crushing
response" to U.S. military aggression by launching six drones targeting a U.S. radar
in Bahrain.
It said it launched this number of drones to ensure the U.S. understands any act of
aggression will be met with a severe response.
Bahrain confirmed the Iranian attack, saying its air defenses intercepted them all.
U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to NPR's request for comment.
The apparent tit-for-tat attacks come as Iran continues attacking oil tankers in the
Strait of Hormuz, including it says two on Sunday with mines.
Ayah Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the hours-long FAA ground stop of all planes
in the U.S. Friday is still snarling air traffic around the country, and he says the investigation
into what happened continues.
Focused on a federal contractor that Duffy says was updating copper wires to digital
fiber ones.
"We're looking at a full suite of issues with the router and with the installation.
Now, we know who did the install, a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran.
So we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install at all.
But we don't actually have the root cause."
Speaking there on CNN's State of the Union, meanwhile, President Trump has now commented
for the first time on the delays that left thousands of travelers stranded over the weekend.
On social media, he blamed former President Biden for FAA funding issues.
On Wall Street, investors are keeping an eye on NVIDIA this week, this time looking past
its former CEO's scandals and toward the chipmaker's earnings.
And Pierre Stephen Basaha reports, investors are also gearing up for the artificial intelligence
company Anthropics' initial public offering.
There has been a pattern over the past few years on the AI side of the stock market.
Investors get worried the industry is overvalued.
Then NVIDIA shares another quarter of jaw-dropping earnings beating Wall Street expectations.
Tuesday, NVIDIA will again report its latest earnings during an especially tough time for
the industry and the company.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ is down about 7.5% over the month.
NVIDIA's stock value has also fallen sharply after the ouster of its scandal-plagued CEO
Jensen Wong last week.
Anthropics is looking to join that shaky stock market with an initial public offering planned
for later this week.
The price Anthropics currently signaling would value the company at $1.4 trillion.
Stephen Basaha, NPR News.
To properly inform users that its Facebook app could access all photos and videos and
the related metadata on Android devices.
The regulator says Facebook's access permissions were not transparent and users did not understand
what they were authorising.
It has instructed Meta to seek consent with separate, specific and clear requests.
The authority also cited Meta's lack of cooperation during the investigation.
The fine comes to about 0.4% of Meta's annual turnover.
For NPR News, I'm Esmé Nicholson in Berlin.
At the weekend box office, Johnny Depp is back on top with Ebenezer, his first studio
movie in eight years.
The Paramount Pictures release took the top spot with an estimated $19 million in ticket
sales with $42 million globally.
This against a reported $38 million production budget.
In second place, the cat in the hat with a million dollars, $11 million, followed by
Godzilla minus zero in third place with $8 million.
And rounding out the top five, Ramayana, Rise of a Legend in its second weekend with $5.5
million and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, you can see everything with just under $5.5
million.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Iran says it launched drones at a U.S. radar in Bahrain, which Bahrain says it intercepted
Iran reports explosions near the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on oil tankers there
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says FAA ground stop snarls air traffic; blames federal contractor's router install
Trump comments on weekend flight delays, blaming former President Biden for FAA funding
NVIDIA stock watched ahead of earnings after CEO Jensen Huang's ouster and Nasdaq slump
Anthropic plans initial public offering this week, signaling a $1.4 trillion valuation
EU regulator fines Meta over Facebook Android app access to photos and videos
Johnny Depp's Ebenezer tops weekend box office with $19 million in ticket sales
